about.description_short: Emera (TSX/NYSE: EMA) is a leading North American provider of energy services headquartered in Halifax, Nova Scotia, with investments in regulated electric and natural gas utilities, and related businesses and assets. The Emera family of companies delivers safe, reliable energy to approximately 2.1 million customers in the United States, Canada and the Caribbean. Our team of 6,800 employees is committed to our purpose of energizing modern life and delivering a cleaner energy future for all. Emera's common and preferred shares are listed and trade on the Toronto Stock Exchange and its common shares are listed and trade on the New York Stock Exchange.

analysis_md:
# EMA — Emera Inc.
v5 run, 2026-10-17. Canadian 40-F filer, reports in CAD under U.S. GAAP; engine converted CAD→USD at period-end ECB rates (fx_conversion in dcf_numbers.json). Market cap $14.302B at $47.72 (nasdaq_quote_api) — in scope (<$40B).

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json, or the cited filing — none are recomputed.

## What it is
A regulated utility holding company headquartered in Halifax: Tampa Electric and Peoples Gas in Florida, Nova Scotia Power, New Mexico Gas, Barbados Light & Power, Grand Bahama Power, and Emera Energy/non-regulated holdings — roughly 2.6 million electric and gas customers. Essentially all earnings are regulated and Florida-weighted (Florida operations contribute roughly 70% of adjusted net income). The growth engine is a $20B 2026–2030 capital plan (record $4.0B planned for 2026, ~80% directed to Florida) supporting guided 7–8% rate-base growth and 5–7% adjusted EPS growth through 2030. Post-period event: on October 6, 2026 Emera and Canadian Utilities announced a predominantly all-share merger (~$72B combined enterprise value, ~$45B combined rate base, Emera shareholders ~60%, close targeted Q3–Q4 2027, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals) — the standalone plan below is what was scored; the merger is a risk/overlay item, not an input.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (40-F via EDGAR, USD-converted, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $1,316,108,720; capex $2,579,631,520 (tag PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment); SBC $65,002,040 — by override, see OVERRIDE (Emera files no SBC expense under any EDGAR tag; the C$89M filed figure converts at the 2025 period-end rate 0.73036).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: −$1,328,524,840 = −$4.43/share** (base_oe_latest_per_share −4.432848982315649). Capex for rate-base growth runs at roughly twice operating cash flow — the defining fact of this name on the conservative definition.
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): **+$1,438,858,810** for FY2025 and +$755,632,470 for FY2024 (FY2023: −$346,535,160) — positive in the last two years because it caps capex at D&A. The two definitions straddle zero, which is exactly the utilities model mismatch: most of Emera's capex is growth capex that enters rate base and earns an allowed return, not maintenance.
- **OE positive 0 of the last 5 fiscal years** on the conservative definition (dcf_numbers.json oe_positive_years_of_last_5: "0/5"), and 0 of the last 10 in the filed history. Conservative OE/share by year (financials_history.csv, with the SBC override): FY2023 −$2.16; FY2024 −$1.43; FY2025 −$4.43.
- **Base used = the engine's normalized base (median of last 3 FY OE/share): −$2.16/share** (base_oe_normalized_per_share −2.163710007304602, with the SBC override applied). No TTM base: ttm.py exited without a result (see STALE_FY below), and no TTM construction could change the sign of the base — H1 2026 ran the same playbook (more than $1.7B of capital deployed in the first half against the $4.0B 2026 plan, year-to-date operating cash flow up 8% year over year per the Q2 2026 release).
- Balance sheet: net debt $15,674,255,960 (dcf_numbers.json) against negative normalized OE — leverage is serviced from regulated cash flows and capital-market access, not from owner's earnings as this model defines them. Share count grows 4.1%/yr (share_cagr 0.04068393518439306; DRIP and at-the-market issuance funding the capital plan), a −4.07pp adjustment already inside the engine's blended growth of 4.13%.

## OVERRIDE — SBC (filing-sourced, bounded authority)
- **The gap:** the preliminary engine run exited 4 with `DATA_GAP:sbc` — SBC missing for fiscal years 2023, 2024, 2025 of the last 3. Emera files no SBC expense figure under any candidate tag in EDGAR companyfacts (sbc_tag blank for every year 2016–2025); the expense is disclosed only by plan in the financial-statement notes.
- **The decision (worker, under the 2026-10-14 bounded override authority, kind "filing"):** judgment.json carries `sbc_override = {value: 89000000, kind: "filing", ack_reason: <below>}`. C$89M is Emera's own disclosed FY2025 stock-based compensation cost from Note 32 of its FY2025 consolidated financial statements (filed as Exhibit 99.3 to the Form 40-F for the year ended Dec 31, 2025, filed 2026-02-23, accession 0001193125-26-062876): compensation cost recognized — ECSPP C$3M + stock options C$3M + employee/director DSUs C$29M + PSU plan C$31M + RSU plan C$23M. The DSU/PSU/RSU plans are largely cash-settled liability plans; their recognized cost is nonetheless a real compensation cost of the period, and treating the full disclosed total as SBC errs conservative. The engine FX-converts the CAD override at each period's end rate (fx_conversion.overrides_converted includes sbc; FY2025 filled value $65,002,040).
- **ack_reason (required because the override is mechanically out of band):** the sanity band anchors on the last FILED value and Emera has never filed an SBC value companyfacts carries (last_filed_value: null), so no in-band value exists. The C$89M is not an estimate — it is the sum of the five compensation-cost figures the filer itself disclosed.
- **Single-value caveat, stated plainly:** one override value fills every untagged year (2016–2025), so earlier years carry the FY2025 figure.
